title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Lodging a Dispute on an Invoice Line
content:
## Scope

Under Demurrage and Detention Free Time, disputing an invoice line is the billed party's own act: the billed party lodges it, not the desk. Where a demurrage line is disputed on the ground that rates or free time were misapplied, the amount placed in dispute is governed by the rules on the disputed amount for demurrage. For every other ground, and for any dispute against a detention line, the figure lodged is simply the one the billed party names.

## The customer's filing tool: `lodge_dnd_dispute_1c3d36b3`

This tool belongs to the customer. The agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to file the dispute; the agent does not file it on the customer's behalf.

**What filing does.** A single dispute is registered against one invoice line of the free-time record, with its ground and the amount disputed. It is marked submitted, stamped with the time of filing, and then awaits the desk's decision. Filing books nothing on the account. The receipt names a new dispute reference, used by the desk when it decides the dispute, and the customer thereafter sees the dispute as submitted.

**Parameters.**

- `dnd_id` — reference number of the free-time record whose line is disputed, as the desk gives it to the customer from the free-time record lookup.
- `invoice_event_id` — invoice reference of the one invoice line under dispute, as the desk gives it to the customer from the account entry lookup.
- `dispute_ground` — the ground, which must be exactly one of:
  - `invoice_issued_late` — the line was issued after the invoicing deadline;
  - `rate_misapplied` — the day rates or the rate class billed are wrong;
  - `free_time_misapplied` — the free days or the day count billed are wrong;
  - `incorrect_event_dates` — the recorded movement dates themselves are contested;
  - `carrier_caused_delay` — the days are attributed to a delay caused by the line;
  - `terminal_closure` — the days are attributed to a closure of the terminal.
- `disputed_amount_usd` — the part of the invoice line that is disputed, in US dollars, a positive figure with two decimals.

**Return.** When filed, the tool replies "Dispute <dispute reference> lodged on invoice line <invoice_event_id> of record <dnd_id>: ground <dispute_ground>, USD <amount> disputed, status submitted.", the amount given in US dollars to two decimals. Where the answer starts with "Error:", no record carries the reference supplied and no dispute has been filed.

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Does lodging a dispute reduce what the customer owes?**
Not by itself; filing books nothing on the account.

**Q: Who states the amount for a dispute about a terminal closure?**
The billed party; on grounds other than misapplied rates or free time the stated amount is lodged as given.
